decision_summary: Retain preparation/route-specific controlled mouse muscle-force evidence, conditional on five-day survival. Persistent atrophy, uncertain 2019 drug-arm allocation/blinding, nominal multiple testing, missing assays, and substantial 2021 electrolyte/mortality harms limit transfer. No universal toxic threshold, safe dose, human/MVA efficacy, or food/retail claim.
preparation_identity: Research D,L-3-hydroxybutyrate sodium salt via twice-daily subcutaneous injection; distinct from R,R/S,S ketone esters, oral products and other cation salts.
comparability_limits: 2019 explicit 50:50 Sigma H6501 weight-based 5 mg/g/day; 2021 D,L Sigma material with catalogue/ratio/purity not reported and fixed daily amounts. Do not silently equate every product detail.
2019 healthy controls pair-fed 6.55 kcal/day; 2021 controls pair-fed 5.8 kcal/day.
No sodium-matched comparator in either study.
2019 figure means/SEM; 2021 medians/IQR; no between-study pooled force estimate performed.

citation.title: Adipose tissue protects against sepsis-induced muscle weakness in mice: from lipolysis to ketones

studies.source_qualified_conclusion: A controlled male-mouse prevention experiment reports higher absolute and CSA-normalized EDL force in day-5 survivors receiving D,L-3HB sodium salt, without preservation of muscle mass. Drug-arm randomization and force-assessor blinding are insufficiently described. A related pending patent and survivor/missing-assay limits qualify the signal; no human, oral/retail or BUB1B/MVA efficacy follows.
studies.scope: Only Study 4 tests the sodium-salt drug intervention. Studies 1 (lean/obese metabolism), 2 (adipose ATGL knockout), and 3 (lipid-rich versus standard parenteral nutrition) inform mechanism/context and are not three additional salt efficacy trials. Full main text read; native source depth is specified separately. Figure 5a/b ketogenesis profiles refer to the preceding obesity/lipid/genetic cohorts, not a salt-versus-glucose exposure endpoint.

preparation.source_dose: 5 mg/g body weight/day, not a fixed 150 mg/day in this paper
preparation.route: Twice-daily 400 µL subcutaneous injections, from day 1 after CLP until sacrifice after day 5
preparation.vehicle: Injection solvent not identified in inspected main or Additional file 7; do not infer Plasmalyte from background intravenous resuscitation.
preparation.comparator: D-glucose A3666 Applichem, 6.25 mg/g/day, reported 0.75 kcal/day, same twice-daily 400 µL SC volume; explicitly isocaloric and isovolumetric. No sodium-matched comparator.
preparation.background: Both septic groups received Olimel N7E mixed PN 5.8 kcal/day from day 1; fluid resuscitation/antibiotics/analgesia. Healthy controls were pair-fed standard chow totaling 6.55 kcal/day for Study 4, not full-fed.

design.animals: Male 24-week-old C57BL/6JRj mice (Janvier); lean septic cohort
design.model: Centrally catheterized CLP sepsis, initial 20-hour fasting/fluid resuscitation, no mechanical ventilation
design.allocation: Supplement explicitly randomizes mice to healthy versus sepsis. An explicit within-sepsis salt-versus-glucose randomization statement is not located; Table 1 is labeled Randomization but gives no allocation method. Do not call the drug contrast a fully documented randomized experiment.
design.blinding: Blinded liver-steatosis scoring by two evaluators is described, but force-assessor/caretaker blinding for Study 4 is not reported.
design.hierarchy: Authors state ex vivo muscle force was the primary endpoint and sample-size basis for day-5 experiments; experiments continued until at least 14 force measurements per group. Prospectively registered hierarchy and full power assumptions not verified.
design.exclusions: Catheter loss, occlusion or dislocation; per-reason numbers not supplied. Reported starting denominators need not include every animal initially handled before exclusions.
design.analysis: One-way ANOVA with Fisher LSD/Student t post hoc after transformations, or Wilcoxon for nonnormal data; two-sided alpha .05. No broader multiplicity adjustment is reported. Do not import 2022 explicit no-correction wording as a 2019 quotation.
design.followup: Five days only; prevention from day 1, not treatment after documented established weakness.

denominators.study_n49: 49 denotes the 15+17+17 surviving/terminal cohort, not initial enrolled n; Table 1 plus healthy group gives 56 included animals.
denominators.force_n45: 15+16+14 specific-force measurements, conditional on survival; one glucose and three salt survivors lack specific-force measurements with no stated reason.
denominators.absolute_force_n: Not separately stated; do not silently assign the specific-force n to the reported absolute-force statistical test.

force_outcomes.endpoint: Absolute maximal isometric tetanic EDL force ex vivo
force_outcomes.source: Results paragraph preceding Figure 6; Figure 5f displays representative traces only
force_outcomes.precision: A genuine reported direct statistical contrast; no tabulated group mean difference/CI and no separate absolute-force assay n.

force_outcomes.endpoint: Specific maximal isometric tetanic EDL force
force_outcomes.p_bound: ≤.01 from ** marker in native Figure 5g; exact pairwise P unstated
force_outcomes.omnibus_p: ANOVA P<.0001 in caption, not interchangeable with the pairwise P
force_outcomes.normalization: Force/estimated muscle cross-sectional area; native axis mN/mm². Methods use CSA=mass/[1.06 mg/mm³ × fibre length], fibre length=0.44×optimal resting length. Caption per-unit-mass wording is imprecise.
force_outcomes.healthy_comparison: Abstract P=.1 compares salt-treated septic mice with healthy controls; nonsignificance does not prove normalization/equivalence.
force_outcomes.precision: No tabulated direct difference or CI; plots are means±SEM, no digitization.

positive_nonfunctional.regeneration: Salt increased Myod1, Myf5, Pcna, Myog and reduced Mstn versus glucose; Figure 6 native markers distinguish pairwise thresholds from caption omnibus values. Hdac4/Hdac5 lower and Mef2c higher; these markers do not establish causal mediation or restored mature muscle.
positive_nonfunctional.atrophy_marker: Fbxo32 upregulation attenuated (Figure 5e ** between septic groups); Trim63 remained elevated without a significant treatment marker.
positive_nonfunctional.lipid_profile: Supplement S3 shows higher plasma triglycerides (P≤.01 marker) and LDL (P≤.05 marker) toward healthy levels; HDL has no significant treatment marker.
positive_nonfunctional.exposure: Additional file 7 reports transient plasma 3HB 2.9 mM at 30 min, 1.1 mM at 60 min and 0.3 mM at 120 min after bolus. No cohort n, variability, concurrent control or enantiomer-resolved curve supplied.

nulls_and_safety.mass: TA and EDL dry mass remained reduced; abstract reports about 25% loss in both septic groups. No significant salt-versus-glucose mass difference in Figure 5c/d.
nulls_and_safety.survival: 17/20 glucose versus 17/21 salt survivors, Table 1 P=.8; no survival benefit or proof of equivalent safety.
nulls_and_safety.illness: Cumulative illness score salt 8.1±1.2 versus glucose 6.5±1.3, P=.2; no significant difference, not no discomfort. Nonsurvivors receive the maximum illness score plus one; this score is not wholly independent of mortality.
nulls_and_safety.other_nulls: PAX7-positive satellite cell density unaffected (global P=.6); no treatment difference in measured autophagy, inflammatory or mTOR-related markers in S4. Fatty-acid-oxidation gene profile and liver TG not significantly different between drug groups; mass/metabolic nulls do not prove lack of all activity.
nulls_and_safety.harms_scope: No systematic electrolyte/acid-base, renal toxicity or long-term safety demonstration in this 2019 treatment cohort. Absence of lipid-PN steatosis is narrower than general salt safety. Sodium and energy contributions are not separately matched by glucose control.
nulls_and_safety.mechanism: Reduced ketolysis-transporter/enzyme expression does not establish absence of substrate oxidation without direct flux studies; regeneration markers are associations, not proven causal mediators.

lineage.reuse: 2021 cholesterol paper PMC8285799 explicitly reuses 2019 absolute-force measurements. Do not credit its force as independent replication.
lineage.assay_mapping: 2019 force n15/16/14 versus 2021 overall cohort captions n15/17/17; exact per-animal assay map remains unavailable.
lineage.other_study: 2021 toxic-threshold experiment separately described; no complete animal-level non-overlap proof from retained lineage sources.

funding_conflicts_notices.conflict: CG, GVdB and LL report inventorship on pending patent PCT/EP2017/081394 related to this manuscript.
funding_conflicts_notices.data: Available from corresponding author on request; no raw data obtained or contact made.
funding_conflicts_notices.notices: No linked correction/retraction in fresh PubMed CommentsCorrections or Crossref update/relation fields on 2026-09-27; metadata check is bounded.

transfer_limits: Laboratory D,L sodium salt via SC injections is not an oral food/retail ketone-salt preparation
No sodium-matched or pure-D versus pure-L contrast
Male mice with acute induced sepsis and PN; not human critical illness, chronic weakness, MVA or BUB1B deficiency
No BUB1B/BUBR1 measurement in inspected main/methods/gene table
No whole-animal grip, walking, exercise endurance, post-treatment recovery or long-term survival endpoint
decision_critical_unknowns: Explicit drug-arm randomization and force-assessor blinding
Assay/exclusion reasons and absolute-force analysis n
Numerical group force differences/CI and multiplicity-adjusted inference
Raw animal crosswalk and independent replication
studies.depth: Complete scientific main/abstract/methods/results/discussion, Table 1, all main captions and disclosures read in official XML; native Figures 5–6 and native S3/S4 read; complete Additional file 7 text and Additional file 6 gene table read. Non-drug native main Figures 1–4 and supplemental S1/S2/S5 not visually appraised.

citation.title: Identification of the toxic threshold of 3-hydroxybutyrate-sodium supplementation in septic mice

studies.interpretation: Retain nominal specific-force benefit at 150/180 mg per day among five-day survivors, alongside persistent atrophy, electrolyte abnormalities already at 150, and greater illness/mortality at higher tested doses. No general safe dose, class-wide toxic threshold, human regimen, or food/retail transfer established.

preparation.name: D,L-3-hydroxybutyrate sodium salt
preparation.designation: D,L material; actual ratio/purity not analytically reported in this paper
preparation.catalogue_batch_purity: Not stated in this paper; earlier H6501 details not imported
preparation.vehicle_concentration_volume: Not reported in inspected main or supplements
preparation.route: Subcutaneous bolus, twice daily from day 1
preparation.per_injection_amount: Daily labels must not be read as per-injection doses. Equal splitting is plausible but no exact split is explicitly quantified.
preparation.comparators: Glucose 187.5 mg/day called isovolumetric/isocaloric; dose-specific calorie matching across the escalation is unverified. No sodium-matched arm.

model_design.animals: 24-week-old male C57BL/6J, mean initial weight 28.9 g ± 0.2 SEM
model_design.support: Fluid 0.3 mL/h for first 20 h, colloid/crystalloid 1:4; twice-daily antibiotics/analgesia; mixed PN 5.8 kcal/day from day 1
model_design.blinding: Caretakers/data collectors blinded; histology two independent scorers with consensus
model_design.design: Adaptive up/down; reference 150 then 300, de-escalated to 225 then 180. Diagram includes hypothetical branches, not all tested arms.
model_design.power_protocol: No formal power calculation or prospective registered protocol/SAP identified in inspected sources
model_design.selection: All terminal assays condition on survival; post-randomization exclusions and varying assay n prevent all-randomized functional interpretation

counts.source: Native Figure 1c; main captions Figures 2-7 and supplementary caption

groups.terminal_assays: Pooled with the single salt300 survivor; separate effects not reported.
Pooled with seven salt225 survivors; separate effects not reported.

exclusions.caution: Figure1 denominators are included post-exclusion denominators, not verified initial randomized counts. Full flow and reasons for missing assays not supplied.

force.endpoint: Ex vivo EDL maximal isometric tetanic specific force on day 5
force.normalization: Absolute force divided by estimated CSA; CSA = muscle mass / (1.06 mg/mm3 × 0.44 × optimal muscle length)
force.caption_issue: Per unit muscle mass is imprecise relative to native axis/Methods
force.high_pooled: No significant difference from placebo or other groups; highly variable eight selected survivors; no separate 225/300 efficacy estimate
force.healthy_comparison: P ≥ .3 reported in abstract is not equivalence/normalization
force.mass: EDL dry mass lower than healthy in every septic arm, without detected treatment rescue
force.precision: No numerically tabulated treatment difference or CI; no digitization
force.functional_boundary: No whole-animal strength, locomotion/endurance, cognition or long-term functional outcome
force.plot_summary: Figure 7 uses medians and interquartile ranges, as stated in its caption.

survival_illness.salt150: 7/23 deaths versus 3/18 placebo; no detected illness/mortality difference versus placebo is not safety equivalence
survival_illness.mortality: 225/300 significantly worse versus 150; 180 versus 150 P = .2. The abstract 30.4%-to-87.5% mortality increase is 150-to-300, not placebo-to-300.
survival_illness.illness_reporting_difference: Abstract gives doubled-dose illness P = .004; native Figure 1b gives 150-versus-300 P = .0008. Statistical test/comparison explanation for difference not supplied.
survival_illness.score_definition: Nonsurvivors are assigned the maximum severity score plus one. The illness score therefore partly incorporates death and is not wholly separate morbidity evidence.

harms_nulls.finding: All salt arms including 150: higher Na, pH, HCO3 and lower K/Cl versus glucose; higher doses further change selected measures. Pooled high reduces brain/lung water; liver/muscle water and aldosterone show no detected salt-dose effect.

High pooled group has greater dentate neuronal-damage scores; CA1/CA3 have no significant group markers. Liver largely null; 180 sinusoidal dilatation significant versus healthy only. No renal histology or cognitive test.

Kim1 higher and Vnn1 lower at 180/high versus placebo. Ngal shows no salt-dose difference. Creatinine salt arms significant versus healthy only, without placebo markers; avoid claiming placebo-controlled creatinine injury or kidney failure.
Plasma TNFα and kidney/liver Tnf show no detected salt benefit. Hippocampal Tnf in high pooled group versus 150: P = .02.

Native narrower than Results prose: 180 has CA3 versus healthy * only, without placebo/dentate marker; high pooled CA3 versus healthy **/placebo § and dentate versus placebo §; CA1 unmarked. Exact P values not supplied.

No placebo differences marked for FFA/glycerol. At 180, Ppara is lower versus glucose (native marker P≤.01) and separately versus 150 (P=.02). Hmgcs2 is lower at 180/high versus glucose. These pathway readouts do not establish functional rescue.

exposure_mechanism.late: Four hours after dose on day 5: treated .17 ± .04 mM versus placebo .19 ± .04, P ≥ .8
exposure_mechanism.limits: Sparse different-day samples, not formal clearance; Methods say early whole blood, Results call it plasma; no enantiomer-separated exposure data.
exposure_mechanism.causality: Sodium-overload mechanism inferred; no matched-Na comparator separates sodium from ketone/formulation effects. External ester-safety comparisons cited by authors do not isolate mechanism here.
exposure_mechanism.sodium_intake_caution: Values retained exactly as printed in the primary Results: 37.05, 45.76, 52.06 and 66.75 mg/day for 150, 180, 225 and 300 mg/day salt, respectively. Internal arithmetic not independently reconciled; no recalculation substituted.

statistics.multiplicity: Correction not reported; do not import the 2022 explicit no-correction statement. Numerous nominal tests.
limits: Small groups and few high-dose survivors
Below 150 untested; no minimum effective dose or universal toxic threshold

funding_notices.funder_role: Authors state agencies did not participate in design/data/interpretation/writing
funding_notices.baxter: Manufacturer of named PN, not listed as funding source in this paper
funding_notices.data: Reasonable request to corresponding author; no raw data obtained
funding_notices.notices: No linked correction/retraction located in fresh PubMed CommentsCorrections (empty), Europe PMC correction list (absent), Crossref update-to/relation (absent/empty), or publisher notice text. Bounded check; not universal absence proof.

lineage_transfer.lineage: References the 2019 finding as confirmed here. No explicit reuse found, but complete animal independence unverified. Confirmed 2019-to-2021 cholesterol force reuse remains context, not repeated efficacy credit.
lineage_transfer.no_mva: No BUB1B/BUBR1 assay, MVA model or rescue endpoint
lineage_transfer.food_retail: Injected research sodium salt under severe sepsis/PN does not establish healthy dietary ketosis or oral retail benefit/harm.
lineage_transfer.clinical: No clinical regimen or dose conversion recommended; no class-wide ketone toxic claim.

lineage.confirmed_reuse: 2019 absolute-force data reused by 2021 cholesterol paper PMC8285799; no extra independent force credit.
lineage.uncertain_nonoverlap: 2021 toxicity describes its own experiment but no complete animal-level independence/non-overlap crosswalk is available.
lineage.context_not_drug_efficacy: 2019 obesity/ATGL/lipid interventions and its Figure 5a/b ketogenesis profiles are not additional sodium-salt drug trials.
lineage.prior_frozen_lineage_source: External primary packet sources2019/lineage.json; binding retained below.

competitiveness.functional_credit: The 2019 reported absolute-force contrast adds useful preclinical evidence beyond normalized force alone. Preserve it despite the figure showing only representative absolute traces; no exact treatment magnitude/CI or absolute-force assay n was reported.
competitiveness.limits: Survivor-only terminal outcomes, persistent atrophy, uncertain 2019 drug-arm allocation/blinding, missing assays, nominal multiple tests and substantial 2021 dose-associated harms prevent a net whole-cohort or clinical claim.
competitiveness.identity: One D,L sodium-salt route assessment retains the two studies with their separate catalog, ratio, control and dose information. No equivalence to oral products, D-only ketones, other cations or esters follows.
competitiveness.mechanism: Neither study isolates sodium from the ketone anion or demonstrates BUBR1 restoration. Marker associations do not establish a necessary rescue pathway.
competitiveness.decision: Retain an exploratory preparation-specific compensation comparison. Niacin/restoration and apitegromab/compensation remain provisional; no head-to-head or MVA superiority is established.
competitiveness.next_evidence: Measured feasible exposure, sodium-matched and preparation-appropriate controls, absolute useful output with survival/starting-unit denominators, renewable reserve and chromosome fidelity. BUBR1 mediation is additionally required only for restoration claims.

remaining_mechanistic_followup.scope: Earlier lineage reading established reuse of 2019 force data; a complete independent mechanistic appraisal of human association, tracer results and causal necessity remains pending. No additional force replication is assigned.

scope.global_completeness: Broader compound enumeration and efficacy review remain incomplete.
scope.clinical_regimen: None proposed; animal exposures are source descriptors.

root_reading.2019: Complete combined and study source qualifications; selected original drug-force paragraph and methods/captions; native Figure 5 all panels, separating prior experiment panels a/b. Not a second complete root scientific-main read.
root_reading.2021: Complete source qualification and combined structured data; selected original illness-score/force text; native Figures 1,2,6,7 all panels. No figure digitization.
root_reading.independent: Independent review read both complete mains and relevant native/supplement sources, with additional child corroboration for 2021. Two precision notes incorporated into this synthesis.

downstream_precision_notes: Both illness scores partly incorporate death.
Ppara 180-versus-glucose P≤.01 is distinct from 180-versus-150 P=.02.
